title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes axiomatize tame topology (Esquisse §5). M is an ambient space with a class 𝓜 of elementary pieces (cells, or 'X ∈ M'). 𝓕 is the set of 'figures': finite unions of elementary pieces, viewed as subsets of M with a stratification. For a figure F, F̃ is its set of elementary constituents (strata), ordered by X ≤ Y. The relations used are: G ≤ F (G is a subfigure, a union of strata of F); G ≪ F (G is a refinement, i.e. a subdivision of part of F); F ≭ G (F and G are 'compatible' or meet tamely: their intersection is a common subfigure; written ≯ in the transcriptions); F ∥ G (F ≭ G and F ∩ G = ∅). The previous page's Prop. 3 says: if F ≭ G and F' ≪ F, there is a canonical G' = G_{F'} = Inf^≪(F', G) ≪ G with G̃' = G̃ ∩ Omb(F'). F' ↦ G_{F'} is monotone and commutes with arbitrary Sup and Inf.

This page:
- Cor. 1: if G ≤ F, the induced refinement is the plain intersection, G' = G ∩ F' (so G̃' = G̃ ∩ F̃'). That is, Inf^≪(G,F') = Inf^≤(G,F').
- Cor. 2 / Prop. 5: let F ≭ G and L = F ∩ G (a common subfigure). Take refinements F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G, and their restrictions F'_L, G'_L ≪ L. Then (a) F' ≭ G' ⇔ F'_L ≭ G'_L, and (b) F' ∥ G' ⇔ F'_L ∥ G'_L. Compatibility of refinements is thus detected on the overlap alone.
- Consequence: if F'_L = ∅ then F' ∥ G' for every G' ≪ G. Taking L = ∅: if F ∥ G then F' ∥ G' for all refinements. This is the deleted Prop. 2b of the previous page, now derived.
- Prop. 4 (gluing of refinements): for F = ⋃ F_i with Raff(F) = {G ∈ 𝓕 | G ≪ F}, the diagram Raff(F) → ∏ Raff(F_i) ⇉ ∏ Raff(F_i ∩ F_j), G ↦ (G|F_i), is exact (an equalizer). Refinements thus form a sheaf on figures for covers by subfigures.
- Cor. 1: applied to the cover of F by its closed strata X ∈ F̃, Raff(F) → ∏_{X∈F̃} Raff(X) is injective. Its image is the compatible families (G_X) with G_Y = G_X|Y whenever Y ≤ X. Hence Raff F = lim_{X∈F̃} Raff(X), a limit over the face poset.
- The margin note says Prop. 5 should come after Prop. 4, since it relies on localization.

Purpose: to build a 'récapitulatif' of formal properties of ≤, ≪, ≭, ∥ before revisiting the axioms on loci, open and multi-open sets, the set-theoretic case, and the theory of segments (next page).
errors: The transcribed Cor. 1 formula 'F' = F ∩ F'' is meaningless. The intended statement is G' = G ∩ F' (consistent with the bracket G̃' = G̃ ∩ F̃').
The corollary 'F' ∥ G' pour tout G ≤ G' must read 'pour tout G' ≪ G'.

No mathematical errors are detectable. The proofs are absent and the statements depend on unstated axioms (tameness and the existence of Inf^≪), so they cannot be fully checked. Prop. 5 implicitly needs F'_L, G'_L to be the restrictions given by Prop. 3 / Cor. 1, which is fine when L ≤ F and L ≤ G.

ideas.what: Induced refinement on a subfigure equals plain intersection (Inf^≪ = Inf^≤ when G ≤ F)
ideas.modern_name: restriction of a subdivision to a subcomplex / induced stratification

ideas.what: Compatibility/disjointness of refinements of two compatible figures is detected on their intersection L
ideas.modern_name: locality of transversality/compatibility of stratifications; refinement of common subcomplex
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in PL / o-minimal cell decomposition theory

ideas.modern_name: sheaf (stack-like) property of subdivisions over a cover by subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; implicit in PL topology and o-minimal geometry (van den Dries)

ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cellular sheaf viewpoint (Shepard 1985, Curry later)

ideas.what: Axiomatic tame topology via relations ≤, ≪, ≭, ∥ on 'figures' in place of open sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (programmatically, Esquisse 1984); o-minimality by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984–86)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces tame topology but not this relational axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a purely order-theoretic axiomatics for tame topology. Its primitives are relations ≤ (subfigure), ≪ (refinement), ≭ (compatibility) and ∥ (disjoint compatibility) on finite unions of cells. In it he proves that refinements form a sheaf, computed as a limit over the face poset of strata. This axiomatic programme was never completed or published, and no later work develops tame topology in this relational form.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers an alternative, site-like foundation for tame or stratified topology. In it, the poset of refinements of a figure behaves like a sheaf over its face poset. This could connect to cellular sheaves, exit-path categories and combinatorial models of o-minimal structures. However, each individual statement is folklore-level.

deep.surprise_reason: The results are formally natural and routine once the axioms are fixed. The interest lies only in documenting Grothendieck's unpublished relational axiomatics for tame topology and the sheaf/limit description of refinements, which are not in the literature but are not deep.
transcription_corrections: 'F' = F ∩ F'' should be 'G' = G ∩ F''.
In Prop. 5 the hypothesis symbol is a crossed relation, F ≭ G (same as ≯/≭ on the neighbouring pages), not 'F ≰ G'. Likewise in a) the relation is ≭, not ≰.
'pour tout G ≤ G' should be 'pour tout G' ≪ G'.
The margin note reads roughly 'devrait venir après prop. 4' with an arrow pointing to the Prop. 5 block.
The left margin by Prop. 4 contains the definition 'Raff(F) = {G ∈ 𝓕 | G ≪ F}'.
